```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# PREREGISTERED QUESTION (fill in, save, THEN knit)
#
#   Are GCH1 and SLC40A1 inversely correlated in normal breast
#   tissue, and is that coupling retained in luminal A tumours
#   and lost in luminal B tumours?
#
#   Primary statistic : partial Spearman rho between GCH1 and
#                       SLC40A1, adjusted for an epithelial-content
#                       score, computed separately in each group.
#   Groups            : GTEx normal breast (female), TCGA breast
#                       adjacent normal, TCGA LumA, TCGA LumB.
#   Prediction        : .....................................
#                       (write it here before knitting)
#   Decision rule     : the tissue study proceeds only if the
#                       adjusted rho is negative in normal breast.
#
#   Already known, unadjusted, from three cohorts:
#     LumA  -0.154 (GSE96058)  -0.089 (METABRIC)  -0.0695 (TCGA)
#     LumB  -0.029 (GSE96058)  -0.040 (METABRIC)  +0.0760 (TCGA)
#     pooled LumA -0.121 (p 4.9e-10), LumB -0.017 (p 0.53),
#     difference p 0.0021
# ============================================================

for (p in c("UCSCXenaTools", "dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")
}
library(UCSCXenaTools); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2)

# ---- every output of this document lands in one folder ----
OUT <- "coupling_prior_output"
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE)
out <- function(f) file.path(OUT, f)

TOIL <- "https://toil.xenahubs.net"
TCGA <- "https://tcga.xenahubs.net"

GENES <- c(
  "GCH1", "SLC40A1",                       # the axis
  "EPCAM", "KRT8", "KRT18",                # epithelial content
  "ADIPOQ", "FABP4", "PLIN1",              # adipocyte content
  "PTPRC",                                 # immune content
  "MKI67"                                  # proliferation, for context
)
set.seed(123)
cat("All output will be written to:\n", normalizePath(OUT), "\n")
```

## 1. Expression, fetched gene by gene rather than downloaded whole

`TcgaTargetGtex_rsem_gene_tpm` is a multi-gigabyte matrix. `fetch_dense_values()`
asks the hub for named rows only, so this is a few seconds rather than an hour.
Values are log2(TPM + 0.001). Spearman is rank-based, so the transform does not
affect any statistic below.

```{r fetch-expression}
expr <- fetch_dense_values(
  host         = TOIL,
  dataset      = "TcgaTargetGtex_rsem_gene_tpm",
  identifiers  = GENES,
  use_probeMap = TRUE          # lets us ask by gene symbol, not Ensembl ID
)
expr <- as.data.frame(t(as.matrix(expr)))
expr$sample <- rownames(expr)
cat("samples returned:", nrow(expr), " genes returned:", ncol(expr) - 1, "\n")
cat("genes the probeMap could not resolve:",
    paste(setdiff(GENES, colnames(expr)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 2. Phenotype, small enough to download whole

```{r fetch-phenotype, message=FALSE}
ph <- XenaGenerate(subset = XenaHostNames == "toilHub") %>%
  XenaFilter(filterDatasets = "TcgaTargetGTEX_phenotype") %>%
  XenaQuery() %>% XenaDownload(destdir = OUT) %>% XenaPrepare()
ph <- as.data.frame(ph)
names(ph) <- make.names(names(ph))
print(names(ph))
head(ph)
```

The columns to look for are the study (`X_study`: GTEX or TCGA), the sample type
(`X_sample_type`), the primary site (`X_primary_site`) and sex (`X_gender`). Column
names vary slightly between Xena releases, so check the printed names above and
adjust the three filters in section 4 if they do not match.

## 3. PAM50 calls for the TCGA tumours

```{r fetch-pam50, message=FALSE}
clin <- XenaGenerate(subset = XenaHostNames == "tcgaHub") %>%
  XenaFilter(filterDatasets = "BRCA_clinicalMatrix") %>%
  XenaQuery() %>% XenaDownload(destdir = OUT) %>% XenaPrepare()
clin <- as.data.frame(clin)
names(clin) <- make.names(names(clin))
print(grep("PAM50|pam50", names(clin), value = TRUE))   # expect PAM50Call_RNAseq
pam <- clin %>%
  select(sample = sampleID, pam50 = PAM50Call_RNAseq) %>%
  filter(pam50 %in% c("LumA", "LumB"))
table(pam$pam50)
```

## 4. Assemble the four groups

```{r groups}
d <- expr %>% left_join(ph, by = "sample")

gtex_breast <- d %>%
  filter(X_study == "GTEX", X_primary_site == "Breast", X_gender == "Female")

tcga_norm <- d %>%
  filter(X_study == "TCGA", X_sample_type == "Solid Tissue Normal",
         grepl("Breast", X_primary_site))

tcga_tum <- d %>%
  filter(X_study == "TCGA", X_sample_type == "Primary Tumor",
         grepl("Breast", X_primary_site)) %>%
  mutate(short = substr(sample, 1, 15)) %>%
  left_join(pam %>% mutate(short = substr(sample, 1, 15)) %>% select(-sample),
            by = "short")

groups <- list(
  `GTEx normal breast`   = gtex_breast,
  `TCGA adjacent normal` = tcga_norm,
  `TCGA Luminal A`       = tcga_tum %>% filter(pam50 == "LumA"),
  `TCGA Luminal B`       = tcga_tum %>% filter(pam50 == "LumB")
)
sizes <- sapply(groups, nrow)
print(sizes)
cat("\nExpected roughly: GTEx several hundred, adjacent normal ~100,",
    "LumA 400-500, LumB ~200.\nA zero means a filter name needs fixing.\n")
```

## 5. Epithelial content, the adjustment that decides the result

Normal breast is largely adipose. Two genes expressed in epithelium will correlate
with each other across samples simply because some samples contain more epithelium,
which would manufacture a positive correlation and mask a negative one. The score
below is the mean z-score of the epithelial markers minus the mean z-score of the
adipocyte markers, computed within each group so that no cross-group normalisation
is implied.

```{r epithelial-score}
z <- function(x) as.numeric(scale(x))
EPI <- c("EPCAM", "KRT8", "KRT18"); ADI <- c("ADIPOQ", "FABP4", "PLIN1")
add_score <- function(df) {
  if (nrow(df) == 0) { df$epi_score <- numeric(0); return(df) }
  epi <- rowMeans(sapply(intersect(EPI, names(df)), function(g) z(df[[g]])))
  adi <- rowMeans(sapply(intersect(ADI, names(df)), function(g) z(df[[g]])))
  df$epi_score <- epi - adi
  df
}
groups <- lapply(groups, add_score)
```

## 6. The four numbers

Partial Spearman is computed as the correlation of the two genes after each has
been regressed, on ranks, on the epithelial score. The unadjusted value is reported
beside it so the size of the adjustment is visible.

```{r correlations}
pspear <- function(df) {
  if (nrow(df) < 20)
    return(tibble(n = nrow(df), rho_raw = NA_real_, rho_adj = NA_real_, p_adj = NA_real_))
  x <- rank(df$GCH1); y <- rank(df$SLC40A1); c3 <- rank(df$epi_score)
  rx <- residuals(lm(x ~ c3)); ry <- residuals(lm(y ~ c3))
  ct_raw <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(df$GCH1, df$SLC40A1, method = "spearman"))
  ct_adj <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(rx, ry, method = "pearson"))
  tibble(n = nrow(df),
         rho_raw = unname(ct_raw$estimate),
         rho_adj = unname(ct_adj$estimate),
         p_adj   = ct_adj$p.value)
}
res <- bind_rows(lapply(names(groups), function(g)
  bind_cols(tibble(group = g), pspear(groups[[g]]))))
knitr::kable(res, digits = 4,
  caption = "GCH1 and SLC40A1: Spearman rho, unadjusted and adjusted for epithelial content")
write.csv(res, out("coupling_prior_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 7. The verdict, read against the prespecified decision rule

```{r verdict}
g <- function(name, col) {
  v <- res[[col]][res$group == name]
  if (length(v) == 0 || is.na(v)) NA_real_ else v
}
gt <- g("GTEx normal breast", "rho_adj")
an <- g("TCGA adjacent normal", "rho_adj")
la <- g("TCGA Luminal A", "rho_adj")
lb <- g("TCGA Luminal B", "rho_adj")

verdict <- c(
  sprintf("GTEx normal breast      adjusted rho = %s", format(round(gt, 4))),
  sprintf("TCGA adjacent normal    adjusted rho = %s", format(round(an, 4))),
  sprintf("TCGA Luminal A          adjusted rho = %s", format(round(la, 4))),
  sprintf("TCGA Luminal B          adjusted rho = %s", format(round(lb, 4))),
  "",
  if (!is.na(gt) && gt < 0)
    "NORMAL BREAST: coupling present. Decision rule met, the tissue study proceeds."
  else
    "NORMAL BREAST: no inverse coupling. Decision rule NOT met, do not start the tissue study.",
  if (!is.na(la) && la < 0)
    "LUMINAL A: coupling survives adjustment. The three-cohort result can go into the manuscript."
  else
    "LUMINAL A: coupling does not survive adjustment. Submit the manuscript unchanged.",
  if (!is.na(lb) && abs(lb) < abs(la))
    "LUMINAL B: weaker than luminal A, consistent with the asymmetry."
  else
    "LUMINAL B: not weaker than luminal A. The finding is about transformation, not subtype."
)
writeLines(verdict)
writeLines(verdict, out("VERDICT.txt"))
```

## 8. Plot

```{r plot, fig.width=7.2, fig.height=5.6}
plt <- bind_rows(lapply(names(groups), function(g)
  groups[[g]] %>% transmute(group = g, GCH1, SLC40A1)))
plt$group <- factor(plt$group, levels = names(groups))
lab <- res %>% transmute(group = factor(group, levels = names(groups)),
  txt = sprintf("n = %d\nrho = %.2f (adjusted %.2f)", n, rho_raw, rho_adj))
p <- ggplot(plt, aes(GCH1, SLC40A1)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(data = lab, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = txt),
            hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.2, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "GCH1 against SLC40A1 in normal breast and in luminal tumours",
       subtitle = "log2(TPM + 0.001), UCSC Toil recompute. Line is ordinary least squares, for display only.",
       x = "GCH1", y = "SLC40A1") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)
p
ggsave(out("coupling_prior.png"), p, width = 7.2, height = 5.6, dpi = 300)
```

## 9. Reading the output

A negative adjusted rho in GTEx normal breast and in TCGA adjacent normal says the
coupling exists in untransformed tissue, which is the premise of the tissue study.

A negative adjusted rho in Luminal A and one near zero in Luminal B reproduces the
three-cohort pattern and makes the tissue study a test of a stated prediction.

A negative rho in both luminal subtypes means the finding concerns transformation
rather than subtype, which is a different paper and still worth writing.

A rho near zero in the normals kills the hypothesis, and that is the most valuable
of the four outcomes, because it costs a week instead of a year.

```{r session}
file.copy("00_coupling_prior.Rmd", out("00_coupling_prior_source.Rmd"), overwrite = TRUE)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), out("session_info.txt"))
cat("\nFiles written to", normalizePath(OUT), ":\n")
print(list.files(OUT))
sessionInfo()
```
